real_task.outcome: Quantify the first-order architecture envelope for 1M, 10M, and 100M payload tonnes/year to approximately 400 km LEO, test prior electromagnetic-launch assumptions, and localize the true scaling residuals.

implementation.model: 2D equatorial inertial point mass + rotating atmosphere + US Standard Atmosphere 1976 + constant ballistic-coefficient drag + Sutton-Graves convective heating + closed-form accelerator/throughput scaling
implementation.scope_warning: Architecture envelope only; not CFD, TPS certification, guidance design, detailed electromagnetic launcher design, or demonstrated system performance.

authoritative_sources.source: NASA Sutton-Graves stagnation-point convective heating relation
U.S. Fleet Forces EMALS dead-load testing
authoritative_sources.use: demonstrated heavy electromagnetic launch mass context: deadloads to 80,000 lb
demonstrated high-speed electromagnetic launch context: 10.64 MJ, 2520 m/s

authoritative_sources.source: Powell, Maise, Rather — StarTram 2010 concept paper
authoritative_sources.use: concept-reference comparison only, not authority for demonstrated performance

corrected_prior_assumptions.prior: 15–20 t payload / ~17.8 t gross / ~4 m diameter was the active Pass-4 pod search region.
corrected_prior_assumptions.correction: For a 6 km near-orbital atmospheric exit, this geometry has poor mass per frontal area. Reaching ballistic coefficient 150,000 kg/m^2 at 17.8 t gross and 4 m diameter would require Cd≈0.0094, far below the 0.05–0.12 drag-coefficient range explored in the StarTram concept study.

corrected_prior_assumptions.prior: Very high throughput implies many parallel accelerator lanes by cadence alone.
corrected_prior_assumptions.correction: Lane count is not set by launch count alone. It depends on pod transit time divided by launch interval. Larger payload pods radically reduce cadence.

corrected_prior_assumptions.prior: ~100 m/s insertion can be assumed after a near-orbital mountain launch.
corrected_prior_assumptions.correction: ~116 m/s is only the ideal tangential no-drag two-body reference from 6 km to 400 km apogee. Atmospheric loss and flight-path angle materially change insertion delta-v.

reference_search_region.sensitivity_warning: Cd, lift/shape, nose geometry, real-gas/radiative heating, angle, and guidance are decisive. Cd=0.05 is an explicit search assumption, not a demonstrated property.

technology_reality_check.demonstrated_heavy_em_launch: EMALS dead-load testing has used carts up to 80,000 lb, but at aircraft-launch velocities.
technology_reality_check.demonstrated_high_speed_em_launch: NAVSEA records a 10.64 MJ electromagnetic railgun firing at 2520 m/s, but at projectile scale.
technology_reality_check.localized_gap: The critical electromagnetic-launch gap is mass × velocity × repetition × reliability together, not proof that any one ingredient exists.
technology_reality_check.tps_context: NASA reports PICA demonstrated capability below 1800 W/cm^2; the reference search point's Sutton-Graves convective peak is about 7050 W/cm^2, so routine reusable/low-maintenance TPS at the required cadence remains unproven and requires a different material/cooling/lifecycle solution.

frontier_capability_note: This real task demonstrates useful components of the frontier behavior, but one domain plus a same-domain parameter reuse cannot prove broad cross-domain frontier capability.
